messages.subject: Weird arrangement of NA's and occurrences with the detectionHistory function
messages.subject_clean: Weird arrangement of NA's and occurrences with the detectionHistory function
messages.body_plain:
Dear Dr. Jorgen, I am coming to you for help with a problem I have experiencing in creating my detection-non-detection matrices using the detectionHistory function in camtrapR. I have searched in previous group discussions but did not find a similar problem.

I performed a CT sampling that started on December 16, 2016 and ended on March 20, 2017. (Below is attached the camera operation matrix)

I accumulated a total of 95 continuous days of sampling and obtained them by means of 30 spatially replicated camera traps at another site, accumulating a total of 61 cameras. Since my sampling was spatially replicated, I would expect my detection histories to have an alternate structure of NA blocks where the sites from the first spatial replicate were not active during the sampling of the second one and vice versa.

At the time of creating the operation matrix, I do not experience any inconvenience and when previewing it I can see that my NA's are distributed accordingly to the start and end dates of each sampling site.

To create the matrix of independent records every 24h I did not experience any problem either. However, when I run the function with the data I obtained independently for each 24h, it occurs that when the matrix comes out, half of its fields appear with 0's and the other half with NA's, which doesn't match with the NA's blocks nor with the detection history that I was spectating.

I attach my version of the script as well as the previously mentioned arrays.

# Load data

data_indp24h<- read.csv("datadep_24h.csv", header = T) # 24h records

actividad_cam <- read.csv("camera_act_UC.csv", header = T) # operation matrix

View(actividad_cam)

#Operation matrix

actividad_cam_2 <- cameraOperation(CTtable = actividad_cam,
stationCol = "Station",
setupCol = "start_date",
retrievalCol = "end_date",
hasProblems = F,
dateFormat = "%d/%m/%Y")

#Create detection history

hist_captura_perspicax <- detectionHistory(recordTable = data_indp24h,                                camOp = actividad_cam_2,
            stationCol = "Station",
            speciesCol = "Species",
            recordDateTimeCol = "DateTimeOriginal",
            recordDateTimeFormat = "%d/%m/%Y",
            species = "Penelope_perspicax",
            occasionLength = 5,
            day1 = "station",
           includeEffort = T,
           scaleEffort = TRUE,
           timeZone = "America/Mexico_City")

#detection history

detecciones <- hist_captura_perspicax [[1]]

duracion <- hist_captura_perspicax [[2]]

Can you give me a hand with the origin of my problem and explain me how I can solve it?

Cheers!

Juan.

messages.body_plain:
Hi Juan,

I had a look at your data and here's what I found.

There were typos in

setupCol = "start_date",

retrievalCol = "end_date",

-> They should both the upper case.

Then I get  camera operation matrix, which looks like you did sampling in two time periods (see attachment, created with camopPlot). That corresponds to the setup/ retrieval dates in your table.

I can't run detectionHistory because of the following error:

"Not all values of stationCol in recordTable are matched by rownames of camOp"

And indeed, the record table has station names like "C1", the camera table has "CT-UC-01-01" etc. So detectionHistory can't match the stations in the record table with the stations in the camera operation matrix and gives an error. That would need to be fixed so the stations match.

Normally you should not even be able to run your script, but receive error messages instead.

In detectionHistory, you should not see these two blocks as in the plot below because you set    day1 = "station". So the detection history at station should begin on the first occasion (first column).  I'm sorry I can't be more specific because I can't run detectionHistory with the data you shared.

Best regards,

Jürgen

messages.subject: raw data organisation for multiple memory cards of a single camera ID
messages.subject_clean: raw data organisation for multiple memory cards of a single camera ID
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,
I´d like to start using the camtrapR workflow but I do have a question concerning the directory structure (i.e. the raw camera trap data organisation) and I did not find relevant information so far.

I do have data from camera traps that operated from spring to autumn without changing their location. During this period the camtraps have been checked several times - including memory card replacements.
In some cases we needed to adjust the internal time of the camera because it was not specified correctly (or malfunction in some rare cases). After adjustment the internal time was (obviously) correct. Therefore only a subset of the images of a camera need adjustment of the time shift.
According to the vignette it is only possible to shift the time of the whole directory of a camera (or a station).
Therefore I´d ask you for any ideas on raw data organisation in such cases.

As a workaround, my idea is to rename the ID of the camera for each memory card replacement using the same coordinates (a combination of camera ID and memory card replacement). Are there any reasons against this approach?

Thanks in advance!

Best regards
Frederik

messages.subject: Re: Multi-scale (Multi-method) detection histories
messages.body_plain:
Hi Evan,

I ended up just manipulating the data frame to produce what I needed. Here is some example code of what I did to convert the standard output from camtrapR (where each camera was a row) into something I could use for RPresence. First, I added a column to the camtrapR operations dataframe output (cameraOperation function) that numbered the cameras per site by grouping by site year and using the row_numbers function. So if there were 3 cameras at a site, then they would get numbered 1, 2, 3 etc. Then I subset that frame to just include the site id and number of cameras. Then I joined that to the detection history data frame based on the site id column. Hopefully you can follow the rest of the pasted code below? As a disclaimer, I suspect there are much more efficient ways to do this, but this is what worked for me.

#Attach the camera number info to the detection history data frame

dh_pred_10 <-
  dh_pred_10 %>%
  rownames_to_column(var = "year_site_camid") %>%
  left_join(., cam_num, by="year_site_camid")

#now subset the data by cam number to set up the wide data frame by "method"
#I had up to 4 cameras per site, so if you only had 2 then you would just need the first 2 chunks etc....

dh_pred_10_1 <-
  dh_pred_10 %>%
  filter(cam_num == 1)

dh_pred_10_2 <-
  dh_pred_10 %>%
  filter(cam_num == 2)

dh_pred_10_3 <-
  dh_pred_10 %>%
  filter(cam_num == 3)

dh_pred_10_4 <-
  dh_pred_10 %>%
  filter(cam_num == 4)

#now join the data frames back together in wide form and add a suffix to the respective observations

df_pred_10 <-
  dh_pred_10_1 %>%
  left_join(.,dh_pred_10_2, by=c("year_site"), suffix=c("","_cam2")) %>%
  left_join(., dh_pred_10_3, by=c("year_site"), suffix=c("","_cam3")) %>%
  left_join(., dh_pred_10_4, by=c("year_site"), suffix=c("","_cam4"))

#now organize the data frames so the occasions are all together, this depends on how many occasions you have but will sort them the way you need them for Presence
dh_pred_10 <-
  df_pred_10 %>%
  dplyr::select(o1, starts_with("o1_"),o2, starts_with("o2_"),o3, starts_with("o3_"),
                o4, starts_with("o4_"), o5, starts_with("o5_"), o6, starts_with("o6_"),
                o7, starts_with("o7_"), o8, starts_with("o8_"), o9, starts_with("o9_"),
                everything())

#subset to replace dots with NAs in the detection history
dh_pred_10_subset <- dh_pred_10[1:36] #grabs only the detection history data, will vary depending on the number of observations and cameras in your data

dh_pred_10_subset <- data.matrix(dh_pred_10_subset)

Hopefully this helpful.

Matt

messages.subject: Re: Multi-scale (Multi-method) detection histories
messages.body_plain:
Hi Matt & Evan,
thank you for sharing your thoughts and the solution. I didn't get to check the code you shared yet and don't use Presence either, but here is a very simplistic idea (my apoligies for shortcomings or misunderstandings.

mat1 and mat2 represent the detection histories for camera 1 and camera 2 of each station respectively (one needs to so some data wrangling first to run detectionHistory for individual cameras instead of both: subsetting the camera trap data frame etc.).  The values below are nonsense and only for illustration of which cell goes where.

mat1 <- matrix(c(1,2,3,4), nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE)
mat2 <- matrix(c(5,6,7,8), nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE)
> mat1
     [,1] [,2]
[1,]    1    2
[2,]    3    4
> mat2
     [,1] [,2]
[1,]    5    6
[2,]    7    8

They can then be combined

mat_comb <- matrix(paste0(mat1, mat2), nrow = 2)
out <-matrix(apply(mat_comb, MARGIN = 1, FUN = paste, collapse = " "))
> out
     [,1]
[1,] "15 26"
[2,] "37 48"

I don't know if a matrix is the correct output. One could also easily convert it to a text file with line breaks with something like:

cat(paste(apply(mat_comb, MARGIN = 1, FUN = paste, collapse = " "), collapse = "\n"))
15 26
37 48

That could be combined with sink() to get a text file.
Best regards,
Jürgen

messages.subject: Re: Multi-scale (Multi-method) detection histories
messages.body_plain:
Thanks Matt and Jürgen for your detailed responses! Both were very useful for writing my own script that got the detection history in the form that works for Presence.

In my case, I'm looking at camera pairs where one is placed on-trail and the other off-trail, so I just had two methods that I'm comparing. As you suggested, I had my camera operation (camOp) dataframe output structured so that every camera had its own row. Using the stationCol and cameraCol arguments, I could identify in my camOp output what station each camera belongs to and whether it was "on" or "off" trail. Making sure that my capture event dataset also had a matching stationCol column for the detectionHistory function, this gave me detection histories also with detection/nondetection data per camera. From there I took a page out of Matt's book and used the script below to separate cameras by "on" and "off" trail placements, combine them into one row while still maintaining method-specific survey columns, and then reordering them so that on and off-trail occasions were organized by survey:

#Isolate detection histories (det_hist) into on and off trail dataframes

det_hist_on <- det_hist[grepl("on", rownames(det_hist)), ]
det_hist_off <- det_hist[grepl("off", rownames(det_hist)), ]

#Add a suffix to the "off" trail dataframe to differentiate occasions
colnames(det_hist_off) <- paste(colnames(det_hist_off), "off", sep = "_")

#Join the dataframes back together as one row (note that this only works if you have the same # and order of cameras by method, i.e 50 cameras from method A, 50 cameras from method B, etc.)
det_hist_2methods <- cbind(det_hist_on, det_hist_off)

#Reorder occasions by survey (o1, o1_off, o2, o2_off, etc.)

det_hist_2methods <-
  det_hist_2methods %>%

  dplyr::select(o1, starts_with("o1_"),o2, starts_with("o2_"),o3, starts_with("o3_"),
                o4, starts_with("o4_"), o5, starts_with("o5_"), o6, starts_with("o6_"),
                o7, starts_with("o7_"), o8, starts_with("o8_"), o9, starts_with("o9_"),

                o10, starts_with("o10_"),o11, starts_with("o11_")...)

I'm also sure that there are much more elegant ways to do this, but this did the trick for me. And thanks again to Matt and Jürgen! This thread really helped me move forward with my analysis.

Eric

Hi Ana,
yes, currently the function stops and throws an error if the target directory is not empty (contains images already). So in the first iteration of your loop it works (when the directory is still empty), in the second iteration it finds images and refuses to continue.
The relevant code it quite old and I believe I added it to avoid accidentally overwriting images that were tagged already (thereby potentially losing the tags). And it also wasn't intended to contain subdirectories by year. The function is not very flexible to be honest.

So I'm sorry to say that in its current state, there is little the function can do out of the box. You could do one of these things:
change the directory structure
modify the getSpeciesImages function (the line that causes the error).
Since you are new to R I did the latter for you. Please source the attached getSpeciesImages function. It is minimally modified and causes a warning instead of an error in your situation (line 52). Please use it carefully since it may overwrite existing images. I also don't know if the function would preserve the year directories you are using. Just try and see, but please make a backup first.

Also run this line first, it loads a few functions that getSpeciesNames needs internally:
devtools::source_url("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jniedballa/camtrapR/master/R/variousOtherHelperFunctions.R" <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jniedballa/camtrapR/master/R/variousOtherHelperFunctions.R>)

Hope this helps. And please let me know how it goes.
All the best,
Jürgen

Hi,
the function imageRename() will rename all images, it does not filter anything. Like you said, the recordTable function does that.

I don't quite understand the question about filtering images before tagging. How would you define the "same time"? Same exact second? Or within a certain time interval of the first
image? Using a time interval would not be safe because usually we can't assume that everything within the next xy minutes (for example) will be the same species. So currently I don't think there's a way get around tagging all images inorder to extract all the information you want.

Just in case you're not aware of it, digiKam can bulk-assign tags to multiple images at once, so you don't have to click them individually. That speeds up the process a lot.
Best,
Jürgen

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I've got data from two studies with the same format- one carried out in 2013 and the other in 2019. I want to merge them together so as to get the input for unmarked.

The way I have tried to do is that I've combined the camera operation matrices and then removed columns with all NAs. And use this and the merged species RT from both studies as the input for obtaining detection histories for individual species. But this leaves me with the error:
Error in camOp[i, as.character(record_dates_tmp[which_tmp])] : subscript out of bounds

I'm unsure how to correct this error.

Also, is this the correct way to approach this? I am able to obtain species detection histories from both studies separately and then combine them to use as the input for unmarked and this works fine. But I'm aiming to run a metadata analysis from multiple studies with the same data collection format, so its easier to merge them as raw data and then obtain detection histories as I'm also running it for multiple species.

Thanks a lot!
